hypothesis: A breeding SiteID that has been abandoned requires a higher surrounding population state to be recolonized than the surrounding population state at which it was abandoned.

competing_predictions.reversible_static_site_quality: H approximately 0 for the same SiteID because occupancy maps reversibly onto population size after stable site quality is paired out.
competing_predictions.history_dependent_or_social_feedback: H > 0 because an empty site loses the state/social advantages of occupancy and recolonization requires greater surrounding population pressure.

abundance_definition.parent_state: leave-one-SiteID-out total abundance within the frozen species x MasterSite panel
abundance_definition.reason: excluding the focal SiteID prevents its own transition from mechanically entering the predictor
abundance_definition.transition_state: mean of log1p leave-one-site-out totals in the two years bracketing the transition

spell_estimand.interpretation: H>0 means spatial recovery requires a higher surrounding population state than spatial loss at the same SiteID

aggregation.step1: average H across multiple completed spells within SiteID
aggregation.step2: average SiteID means within species x MasterSite
aggregation.step4: primary T = unweighted mean of species means

primary_inference.observed_statistic: T_obs = unweighted mean of species mean H after spell -> SiteID -> MasterSite -> species aggregation

sign_flip.null: species-level H means are symmetric around zero
sign_flip.test: one-sided sign-flip randomization of species means

trajectory_drift_null.purpose: Rule out positive H caused only by the fact that recolonization occurs later on a changing parent-abundance trajectory.
trajectory_drift_null.per_spell: Uniformly sample one frozen pseudo start year from that spell's precomputed eligible pseudo placements. Preserve SiteID, panel, exact transition-gap years, and the observed leave-one-SiteID-out parent abundance trajectory.
trajectory_drift_null.pseudo_H: Compute the same difference between later and earlier transition-midpoint log1p parent states at the pseudo placement.
trajectory_drift_null.aggregation: Use the exact same spell -> SiteID -> MasterSite -> species -> equal-species hierarchy as T_obs.

primary_inference.support: Require T_obs > 0, sign-flip one-sided p <= 0.05, Delta_T > 0, and trajectory-drift-null upper-tail p <= 0.05.

secondary_uncertainty.reporting: report species means, MasterSite means, SiteID means, all spell-level H values, and the full trajectory-drift-null summary

boundaries: A positive H is evidence of history-dependent spatial recovery, not proof of an Allee mechanism.
Site pairing controls stable SiteID quality but not time-varying habitat degradation, predator change, disturbance or unmeasured management.
Do not call the result social hysteresis unless independent social-cue or fitness-density evidence is added.
Do not use first colonization events in the primary threshold comparison.
Do not change the completed-spell roster after count magnitudes are opened.
The structured trajectory-phase null calibrates generic temporal alignment but does not remove time-varying habitat quality.
The trajectory-drift null controls generic change in surrounding abundance over the same elapsed time but is not a complete mechanistic model of reversible habitat selection.
stop_rule: One execution only after the support gate passes. No alternative abundance transform, lag, transition midpoint, pseudo-placement rule, null family, site subset, minimum vacancy duration, species subset or weighting rule may be added after H is opened.

trajectory_phase_null.purpose: Calibrate whether positive H could arise from generic alignment with the observed long-term parent-abundance trajectory, annual sampling, or overshoot rather than asymmetric recovery.
conditioning: exact frozen completed-spell roster and transition years
observed multivariate count trajectory within each species x MasterSite
contiguous complete-year block containing each spell
trajectory_phase_null.randomization: Within each species x MasterSite contiguous complete-year block, apply one common circular year shift to the entire count matrix. Use the same shift for every focal SiteID/spell in that block, preserving cross-site covariance. Keep spell transition years fixed.
trajectory_phase_null.p_value: plus-one upper-tail probability that shifted species-balanced T >= observed T
trajectory_phase_null.interpretation: This is a structured alignment null, not a fitted mechanistic occupancy model.
